claims.quote: However, cardiac tamponade is primarily a clinical diagnosis. Pearls & Pitfalls Significant cardiac tamponade is a clinical diagnosis; echocardiographic findings alone are not an indication for pericardiocentesis.

claims.text: ECG: low voltage and electrical alternans suggest tamponade but lack sensitivity and specificity
claims.quote: Low voltage and electrical alternans on the ECG suggest cardiac tamponade, but these findings lack sensitivity and specificity (6).

claims.text: If suspected but not confirmed, right heart (Swan-Ganz) catheterization may be done: in tamponade there is no early diastolic dip, diastolic pressures are elevated (approximately 10 to 30 mm Hg) and equal in all chambers and the pulmonary artery, and the x descent is preserved while the y descent is lost
claims.quote: If tamponade is suspected but not yet confirmed (eg, by clinical findings and echocardiography), right heart (Swan-Ganz) catheterization may be performed. In cardiac tamponade: There is no early diastolic dip in the ventricular pressure record. Diastolic pressures are elevated (approximately 10 to 30 mm Hg) and equal in all cardiac chambers and in the pulmonary artery. In the atrial pressure curve, x descent is preserved and y descent is lost.

claims.text: Causes A moderate or large pericardial effusion impairs cardiac filling, lowering cardiac output; with rapid accumulation (usually blood), even small amounts (eg, 150 mL) may cause tamponade, while slow accumulation of up to 1500 mL may not
claims.quote: Cardiac tamponade occurs when a moderate or large pericardial effusion impairs cardiac filling, leading to low cardiac output and sometimes shock and death. If fluid (usually blood) accumulates rapidly, even small amounts (eg, 150 mL) may cause tamponade because the pericardium cannot stretch quickly enough to accommodate it. Conversely, slow accumulation of up to 1500 mL may not cause tamponade.

claims.text: Acute pericarditis may result from infection, autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, uremia, injury or surgery, MI, cancer, radiation therapy or certain medications
claims.quote: Acute pericarditis may result from infection, autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, uremia, injury or surgery, myocardial infarction (MI), cancer, radiation therapy, or certain medications (see table ).

claims.text: Post-MI: occasionally the heart ruptures, causing hemopericardium and tamponade, usually 1 to 10 days after MI and more commonly in females
claims.quote: Occasionally, the heart ruptures post-MI, causing hemopericardium and tamponade, usually 1 to 10 days post-MI and more commonly in females.

claims.text: Symptoms Similar to cardiogenic shock: decreased cardiac output, low systemic arterial pressure, tachycardia and dyspnea, but with markedly dilated neck veins
claims.quote: The clinical findings of cardiac tamponade, also called pericardial tamponade, are similar to those of cardiogenic shock: decreased cardiac output, low systemic arterial pressure, tachycardia, and dyspnea. However, neck veins are markedly dilated.

claims.text: Severe tamponade is nearly always accompanied by pulsus paradoxus (systolic BP falls > 10 mm Hg during inspiration), and in advanced cases the pulse may disappear on inspiration; pulsus paradoxus can also occur in COPD, asthma, PE, RV infarction and noncardiogenic shock. Heart sounds are muffled unless the effusion is small
claims.quote: Severe cardiac tamponade is nearly always accompanied by a fall of > 10 mm Hg in systolic blood pressure during inspiration (pulsus paradoxus). In advanced cases, pulse may disappear during inspiration. (However, pulsus paradoxus can also occur in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD], bronchial asthma, pulmonary embolism, right ventricular infarction, and noncardiogenic shock.) Heart sounds are muffled unless the effusion is small.

claims.quote: Except in emergencies (eg, cardiac tamponade), pericardiocentesis, a potentially lethal procedure, should be performed using echocardiographic guidance in a cardiac catheterization laboratory and should be supervised by a cardiologist or thoracic surgeon if possible.
